apparatus.basis: Standard Kephalaia opening formula ⲧⲧⲁⲗⲓⲛ ⲁⲛ ⲁⲥϣⲱⲡⲉ ⲛⲟⲩⲥⲏⲩ ⲡⲫⲱⲥⲧⲏⲣ ⲁϩⲍⲙⲉⲥⲧ — restored by editor.
Visible [ⲙⲛ] in transcription end of line 6; the listing pattern (with affliction... with misery... with evil... [and a] rest...) requires the conjunction + indef. article.
[ⲙ]ⲏⲧⲓ; the ⲙ continues from line-end ⲉⲓ to form ⲉⲓⲙⲏⲧⲓ (εἰ μή τι 'except, unless').
ⲛⲉⲛⲧ[ⲟ] line-end; continues to ⲗⲁⲩⲉ in line 10 = ⲛⲉⲛⲧⲟⲗⲁⲩⲉ 'commandments' (Greek ἐντολαί + Lyc. plural).
[ⲗ]ⲁⲩⲉ continues ⲛⲉⲛⲧⲟⲗⲁⲩⲉ from line 9.
ⲛⲍⲏ[ⲧⲥ ⲍ]ⲙ̄ⲡⲱⲕ — the bracketed portion completes ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧⲥ̄ 'in her' and gives ⲍⲙ̄ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧ 'in the purpose of heart' (in glossary).
ⲧⲉ[ⲕ]ⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ; ⲕ restored to complete the standard noun ⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ.
ⲱⲁⲩ[ⲛⲟⲩⲍ]ⲙⲉ — habitual + Lyc. ⲛⲟⲩⲍⲙⲉ 'save' (= Sah. ⲛⲟⲩϩⲙ̄, in glossary). The continuation ⲙⲉ confirms the verb.
ⲛ̄[ⲥⲉ]ⲙⲧⲁⲛ — conjunctive 3pl + ⲙⲧⲁⲛ 'rest themselves'; the ⲙ at line-end joins ⲧⲁⲛ on line 15.
ⲛ̄ⲥⲉ[ⲃⲱⲕ] ⲁⲡⲛⲟⲩⲧⲉ 'and they go to God'; standard Coptic conjunctive of motion-verb completing the sense.
ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲛⲙⲧ[ⲁⲛ] — completes ⲙⲁⲛⲙⲧⲁⲛ 'place of rest' (= ⲙⲁⲛ-ⲙ̄ⲧⲟⲛ); the same compound recurs unbroken in lines 21 and 25.
[ⲡⲉ]ⲥⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲟ — ⲥⲧⲁⲓⲟ 'honor' (in glossary as ⲡⲉϩⲥⲁⲓ̈ⲧ-related; here Sah.-style ⲧⲁⲓⲟ); the feminine possessive ⲡⲉⲥ- 'her (= the church's)' fits the syntactic context.
ⲉⲧⲉⲱⲁⲥⲭⲱ[ⲃⲉ] — completion of habitual relative on ⲭⲱⲃⲉ (Lyc. with ⲭ for ϫ; tentatively read as receive/draw, see notes).
[ⲙⲉ]ⲛⲟⲥ — completes ⲕⲁⲧⲏⲭⲟⲩⲙⲉⲛⲟⲥ 'catechumens' continuing from previous line.
[ⲡⲟⲩⲁ]ⲉ — Lyc. ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲉ 'the farmer' (in glossary); confirmed by full occurrence as subject of the parable in line 30.
[ⲉⲓ]ⲥ — standard Coptic ⲉⲓⲥ 'behold,' demonstrative-narrative marker introducing the next clause about the tree.
[ⲡ]ⲓⲱⲏⲛ — completes the demonstrative ⲡⲓⲱⲏⲛ 'that tree.'
[ⲡⲟⲩⲁ]ⲉ ⲉⲧ]ⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲩ — restoration of 'the farmer there' parallels the structure ⲡⲓⲱⲏⲛ ⲉⲧⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲩ 'that tree' in line 28.
[ⲧⲁⲛ ⲙⲙⲁϩ] — completes ϩⲙ̄ⲧⲁⲛ from line 30 ('of rest') and adds the standard Lyc. locative ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϩ 'there' that closes the parable's first half before the leer-break.
[ⲥⲓⲁ ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲃⲉ ⲧⲛⲧⲁⲛⲧ] — completes ⲧⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲃⲉ 'the holy church' (recurring throughout this kephalaion) plus ⲧⲛⲧⲁⲛⲧ 'is likened' (cf. the rhetorical ⲧⲛⲧⲁⲛⲧ ⲁⲉⲩ in line 26 introducing the simile).
Trailing fragment ⲛⲓⲧ at start of line 1 = end of ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲓⲧ 'beautiful' carried over from end of previous page (p. 217). Standard Lyc. word-break across line/page boundaries.
Editor restoration; ⲁⲡⲡⲉⲓⲁⲏ would be unattested — ⲉⲡⲡⲉⲓⲁⲏ 'in/at the end' is the standard Lyc. expression (cf. l.4).

Editor restoration completing ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲁⲃⲉ from l.9, then continuing with the rest of the sentence.
Editor restoration; ⲯⲩⲭⲏ continues from page edge — single character completion of standard Greek loanword.
Editor restoration; ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ 'living' modifying ⲯⲩⲭⲏ is the standard Manichaean phrase ⲧⲯⲩⲭⲏ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ 'the living soul' (cf. accumulated vocabulary).
Editor restoration; ⲁⲃⲱⲕ ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ 'to go upward' is the standard Manichaean ascent-idiom.
Editor restoration completing ⲥⲥⲁⲩⲛⲉ ⲛ̄ⲥⲣ̄ⲁⲓⲥⲑⲁⲛⲉ 'she knows and-she-perceives'; standard verbal-coordination.
Editor restoration of ⲉⲙⲏⲧⲓ 'except' — Greek-origin exceptive (parallel l.20 ⲉⲓⲙⲏⲧⲓ in same usage).
Editor restoration; ⲍⲛ̄ ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛⲉⲓ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'in the going-forth' completes the spatial-modal phrase governing the gate-imagery.
Editor restoration; ⲡⲏⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲛⲉⲥⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'the house of her men' parallels l.12 and l.24 (same phrase).
Editor restoration; ⲡⲕⲁⲍ ⲙⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ 'the land of light' completes from l.21-22.
Editor restoration; ⲁⲧⲡⲏⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲛⲉⲥⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'unto the house of her men' standard formula (cf. l.12, l.18-19).
Editor restoration completing ⲛⲙⲫⲱⲥⲧⲏⲣ ⲛ̄ⲙ̄ⲡⲧⲏⲩⲉ 'the luminaries of the heavens' from l.16, l.19.
Editor restoration; ϣⲁⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ 'forever' is the standard doxological terminus completing l.27.
Editor restoration completing ⲧⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲁⲃⲉ 'the holy church' (carried to l.28); standard formula recurring throughout the page.
Editor restoration completing ⲕⲁⲧⲏⲭⲟⲩⲙⲉⲛⲟⲥ from l.28 to l.29.
Editor restoration; ⲛⲏ ⲙⲛ̄ ⲛⲉⲓ̈ 'these (= former category) and these (= latter category)' is a standard Coptic enumerative pair-formula.
Editor restoration; ⲡⲉ ⲡⲧⲕⲁⲍ ⲙⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ 'is the land of light' completes the closing identification (l.31-32) which is the chapter's culminating thesis.

notes.decision: Chapter number 87. The pattern ⲡ̄ⲍ̄ ... ⲡ̄ⲍ̄ at line 32 brackets the chapter title with decorative repetition of the numeral, a standard Kephalaia formatting device.
Translated 'a place of life in the Church' — the chapter heading characterizes Mercy as the vital principle within the ecclesiastical body. ⲙⲁ ⲛⲱⲛⲍ̄ = standard Coptic 'place of life.'

Translated 'he spoke to'; analyzed as Lyc. variant of ⲡⲉϫⲁϥ-form combined with dative — likely ⲡⲉϫⲉ + ⲛⲉϩ (3pl dative) functioning as 'he said-to-them.' Cf. accumulated ⲡⲁⲭⲉϩ, ⲡⲧⲁⲭⲉ 'he said.' Could alternatively be 'he inquired of' if root is ϫⲛⲉ 'ask.'

Rendered 'rest at the inward gate.' The phrase appears in a list of negative experiences (affliction, misery, evil); 'rest at the inward gate' likely captures the sense of an inward, secret rest accessible only after passing through outward suffering — the catechumens experience an inward refuge while being pressed externally. ⲣⲟ ⲉϩⲟⲩⲏⲛ literally 'mouth/gate inward.' Reading uncertain.

Translated 'they take a way to go.' ⲃⲛ̄ analyzed as Lyc. for ⲃⲓ/ⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'bear, take' (cf. accumulated ⲁⲓ̈ⲃⲛ 'I bore'); ⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲱ tentatively read as 'a way' (= ϩⲓⲏ) given the immediately following infinitive ⲁⲃⲱⲕ 'to go.' Alternative: ⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲱ as 'a moment' is also possible.

Rendered 'the time, then.' ⲃⲉ taken as discourse particle (cf. δέ-like usage). Could also be ⲡⲥⲁⲡⲃⲉ as a fixed phrase 'in due time / at length,' but the discourse-marker reading fits the syntactic context better.

Translated 'stronghold.' Lyc. variant of ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲟⲣⲉ 'stronghold/fortress' (in glossary), with ⲗ/ⲣ liquid-cluster expansion of ⲭⲣ. Distinguished from homophonous ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲗⲟⲡⲉ 'place of deceit' by context (positive cosmological role of the church) and by the final -ⲣⲉ vs. -ⲡⲉ.

Translated 'she habitually receives.' ⲭⲱⲃⲉ tentatively read as Lyc. reflex of ϫⲡⲟ 'acquire, receive' or related; the construction ⲛⲧⲟⲟⲧⲟⲩ 'from their hand' fits the receiving-sense (church receives her honor through the catechumens' hand). Could alternatively render as 'she habitually depends upon' or 'is sustained by' if from ϫⲱⲃⲉ 'be weak/dependent.'

Translated 'a tilled land' (literally 'a land of tilling/plowing'). ⲟⲩϩⲉ analyzed as Coptic ⲟⲩⲱϩⲉ 'cultivated field, plowing.' Direct correspondence with the agricultural-apostolic typology of this section (cf. accumulated ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲉ 'farmer').

Translated 'habitually moves/changes.' ⲱⲁϩ- as Lyc. habitual prefix (cf. accumulated ϣⲁϩ-); ⲡⲱⲛⲉ from ⲡⲱⲱⲛⲉ 'turn, change, transform.' The tree alters/transforms the power of all the land — fits the agricultural-typological register where the planted tree changes the field's character.

Tentatively rendered 'they bring forth, bringing forth.' Reduplicated/intensive verbal construction of uncertain root; possibly Lyc. for a producing/bearing verb (cf. ⲡⲓⲣⲉ 'bring forth, manifest' in derived sense). The line is the closing application of the simile, where the church 'brings forth' a tree paralleling the field's produce. Etymology uncertain; flagged for parallels.

Treated as the trailing syllable of ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲓⲧ 'beautiful' carried over from the previous page; manuscripts regularly break words across line/page boundaries without hyphenation. The full sense is supplied in the apparatus.

Translated as 'she herself receives unto herself the holy church.' The catechumen-gathering (ⲧⲥⲁⲩⲍⲥ̄, fem.) is the subject; the church is the object. The catechumens are the soil-substrate that hosts the Church, paralleling the agricultural metaphor of land receiving seed.

Translated 'she makes firm for her' on the assumption that ⲣ̄ⲧⲁⲕ is Lyc. ⲣ̄-ⲧⲱⲕ 'do firmness, make firm/strengthen.' The parallel construction with ⲛⲉϯⲙ̄ⲧⲁⲛ ⲛⲉⲥ 'gives rest to her' supports a positive supportive sense. Alternative reading 'establishes' is also possible.

Translated 'her struggles' from Greek loanword μάχη 'battle/struggle' (with Lyc. orthographic ⲍ for χ-elision). Plural with possessive prefix. Fits the ascetic register paralleling 'works' (ⲍⲃⲏⲩⲉ) in line 6.

Translated 'in an agreement of the days' tentatively, taking ⲡⲟⲟⲩⲉ as Lyc. plural of ⲡⲟⲟⲩ 'today/day.' The phrase indicates the soul standing firm in unity for the appointed span of days. Alternative readings ('agreement of evils/labors') possible but less contextually fitting.
Translated 'defilers' as ⲣⲉϥ-ⲗⲱϫϩ̄ 'one who defiles' (cf. accumulated vocabulary ⲗⲱⲭⲍ̄). The cosmic powers other than sun/moon are characterized as defilers of the ascending soul.

Translated 'they become for her a gate open' rather than 'they reign for her open.' Here ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ is the verbal idiom ⲣ̄- ('act as') + ⲣⲟ ('gate, mouth'); the masculine qualitative ⲉϥⲟⲩⲏⲛ 'open' agrees with ⲣⲟ (masc.). Distinguished from line 29 (ⲛⲥⲉⲣ̄ⲣⲟ ⲛⲍⲏⲧϥ 'they reign in it') where the verbal idiom is ⲣ̄- + ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ ('king/kingship').

Translated 'that which is theirs indeed.' ⲡⲧⲱⲩ taken as Lyc. ⲡⲱⲩ 'their (own thing),' with prosthetic ⲧ-. The Land of Light is identified as the proper inheritance of the souls/luminaries. Alternative reading 'that which is the Mountain' (ⲧⲱⲩ = ⲧⲟⲟⲩ) is plausible given the Manichaean 'Mountain of Light' tradition but fits less smoothly here.

Translated 'a final receiver' from Greek loanword ὑποδοχεύς 'host, receiver,' modified by Lyc. ⲛⲍⲁⲏ 'final, last' (= ϩⲁⲏ 'end'). The Land of Light is the eschatological receiver of the cosmic luminaries.
